interpretation: On12 valid varied layouts per seat,412 won24/24,254 won14/24 and146 won2/24. All three lost all32 original-scenario games. This supports spatial transfer beyond the old nearby-town coordinate within this authored easy subset, not broad original-map strategy or a learned recruit-then-attack sequence.
limitations: The initial cohort planned16 easy layouts per seat. Four had off-board native hero visitable positions; two attempted startup failures are unscored and22 affected entries remain unstarted. Maps/seeds were not changed after outcomes. Valid easy comparison has12 matched layouts per seat.

The eight gate games represent four matched old starts, not transfer. The first36 valid transfer games used embedded; the remaining132 used accepted original cold. All36 embedded policy histories also reconstructed exactly under original cold source.
Both runtimes crashed on the same invalid authored fixture. This is not evidence of an acceleration-specific regression. The original strict narrow gate passed and remains unchanged.

Original-scenario results cover one fixed hero-management-v2 board with16 seeds per seat, not a population of layouts. Nominal Wilson intervals describe these fixed tested cohorts; no universal win-rate claim.
Embedded reuse was bounded at two gate games and one transfer game per process. Long-run memory plateau and PPO throughput remain unproven.
Recruitment and army-operation counts are actions, not unique units or causal strategy evidence; attacker role alone does not distinguish neutral from opponent targets.
next_curriculum_proposal: A separately authorized bridge curriculum should retain varied positions while adding an owned learner town and an active opponent hero on a short open board. Gradually approach the original army/economy conditions, keep original-map retention checks, terminal-only rewards and unchanged sampling. Validate native hero visitable offsets before any future cohort. No training is authorized by this diagnostic.
